entities.title: Meet Hosna Ara
entities.summary: Hosna Ara works across AI, data analytics and business intelligence. She is a Master of Information Technology and Systems candidate at the University of Tasmania, with nearly four years of professional analytics and BI experience and research spanning grounded AI, human–AI interaction and interpretable deep learning.

entities.title: Start a conversation
entities.summary: Contact Hosna at hosna.a.bgm@gmail.com for professional opportunities and research collaboration. Explore her public work on GitHub or connect on LinkedIn.

entities.title: Master of Information Technology and Systems
entities.summary: University of Tasmania, Australia. Specialisations in Data Analytics and Artificial Intelligence and Cybersecurity. Cumulative GPA: 6.25/7.00; 2026 GPA: 6.75/7.00. The degree is in progress, with completion expected in December 2026.

entities.title: BSc in Computer Science and Engineering
entities.summary: International Islamic University Chittagong, Bangladesh. Graduated Summa Cum Laude with a CGPA of 3.769/4.00. Undergraduate research investigated computational microwave imaging for post-stroke screening.

entities.title: Business Intelligence Engineer · EBIW Analytics
entities.summary: Developed analytical and reporting solutions using Power BI, DAX, Power Query, SQL, data modelling and reporting automation. Translated operational requirements into dashboards, analytical models and decision-support outputs for business stakeholders.

entities.title: Data Analytics Engineer · eGeneration Ltd
entities.summary: Built and delivered 50+ Power BI dashboards and analytical reports across government and enterprise projects. Work included SQL reporting, KPI analysis, data transformation, visualisation and contributions to data-quality and BI/data-engineering workflows. Data Analytics Engineer was her final role at the organisation.

entities.title: UTAS Research Degree Assistant
entities.summary: Independently built a grounded conversational assistant for discovering research projects, supervisors, scholarships and research-degree guidance. Combines hybrid retrieval with knowledge graphs, relational queries and citation-aware answers. An unofficial student-built prototype; visitors should verify guidance with official UTAS sources.
entities.source: CV, selected projects; public repository README, checked 2026-09-27

entities.title: ThreatBrief AI
entities.summary: An automated threat-intelligence prototype built by the winning team at the TasNetworks Open Innovation Hackathon 2026. Hosna contributed analysis, project coordination and the final presentation. After the hackathon she independently recreated and extended the AI and solution architecture to deepen her understanding of the pipeline and agent workflow.

entities.title: CyberQuiz Pro
entities.summary: An adaptive cybersecurity practice platform developed by a six-member University of Tasmania MITS capstone team. As Project Manager / Communication Lead, Hosna led planning, stakeholder communication, requirements traceability, architecture coordination and delivery management.

entities.title: TasEnergy Insight
entities.date: In progress · public repository checked Sep 2026
entities.summary: A portfolio analytics project exploring Australian electricity-market data for energy operations and decision support. The public README describes project setup and business analysis as in progress; proposed work includes dimensional modelling, SQL and Power BI reporting. The business scenario is fictional, not a client engagement.

entities.title: Ethical issues in human–AI interaction
entities.summary: A PRISMA-guided systematic review of 30 studies spanning digital humans, conversational agents and social robots. Work includes structured extraction, quality assessment and thematic synthesis, examining bias, privacy, safety and the gap between ethical principles and actionable design guidance. Final manuscript draft; not listed as a published paper.

entities.title: Interpretable deep learning for brain tumour classification
entities.summary: First-author research comparing a custom CNN with DenseNet121, VGG16 and ResNet50 using 7,023 brain MRI scans. DenseNet121 achieved 92% validation accuracy in the reported study. Grad-CAM, regional analysis and severity scoring supported interpretation. This is a research result, not evidence of clinical deployment.
entities.role: First author; conceptualisation, experimental analysis, interpretation and manuscript preparation

entities.title: Microwave imaging for stroke screening
entities.summary: Co-developed a computational microwave-imaging framework for post-stroke screening using tissue dielectric-property differences, CST antenna/head-phantom simulation, signal analysis and MATLAB image reconstruction.
